svg.text: FashionSearch Architecture — Mapped to Kreuzberger et al.'s MLOps Framework
Fashion visual search — two pretrained models imported, not trained; GPU work on Kaggle, governance on Databricks
A · Product Initiation Zone — config.yaml, one file
and wants to buy the jacket in it.
B · Data Engineering Zone — Kaggle GPU, then Unity Catalog
10,000 products embedded in 2.5 min on a T4 — 45 min on serverless CPU
Requirements for the feature engineering pipeline
Split by product_id, never by row.
C · ML Experimentation Zone — import by default, fine-tune on demand
model engineering — the pipeline does not care whether a version arrived by download or by training
ML metadata store — one MLflow run per gate evaluation; slice_metrics.json and gate_report.json logged
Training compute — Kaggle T4 GPU. Databricks serverless CPU never loads a model: it reads Parquet.
Repository · GitHub saaspace2/fashionsearch · 71 tests · a push triggers workflows 1 and 2 simultaneously
so reporting survives a blocked gate
only a human moves the rest, and every move is logged with a name.
D · Automated ML Workflow Pipeline — runs once a model holds @production
one row per slice per version
The endpoint runs the COMBINED model: a photo in, one row per garment out.
The app uploads, calls it, and ranks against catalogue vectors locally —
one matrix multiply. The catalogue is never encoded online.
Feedback Loop — enables continuous training, retraining and improvement
08 — coverage, index freshness, champion trend, online quality.
11 — PSI, Jensen-Shannon distance, embedding centroid shift.
Workflow 4 runs nightly at 03:00 UTC and reads the job's exit code:
a high-severity alert means drift, and re-pushes the Kaggle kernel.
Drift detected → workflow 4 re-pushes the Kaggle kernel → a fresh GPU run
→ GitHub registers a new version → the pipeline evaluates it per slice.
Eight steps, nobody in any of them.
A clicked result is a free positive pair; results shown above it and
skipped are hard negatives. Zero labelling cost, real query distribution.
Where this differs from the framework
Zone C normally contains model training. Here both models arrive already trained, so the zone runs import,
validation and export — with fine-tuning available as one flag on the Kaggle side. Two arrows are unusual and
deliberate: GPU work runs on Kaggle because 10,000 embeddings take 2.5 minutes there and 45 on serverless CPU;
and GitHub registers the models because doing it from inside a Databricks notebook is denied on this tier.
FIGURE — adapted. End-to-end architecture of the FashionSearch visual search pipeline, mapped onto Kreuzberger, Kühl & Hirschl's end-to-end MLOps
architecture and workflow (Fig. 4, Machine Learning Operations (MLOps): Overview, Definition, and Architecture, IEEE Access, 2023).
